    Score a parametrised probability distribution

    prediction_scores.Rd

    Create a basket of scores for a set of paramtrised probabilistic predictions compared to a known ground truth, predictions are assumed to be distributional and associated with a link function that transforms them to linear space.

    prediction_scores(df = i_comparison, summarise = TRUE, threshold = NA_real_)

    Arguments

    df

    input dataframe - a dataframe with columns:

    • true_value (numeric) - the true value

    • link (character + default("identity")) - a transformation that puts the quantity being estimated on a linear scale

    • location (numeric) - the location parameter is the estimator mean or median (i.e. the central estimate)

    • scale (numeric) - the scale parameter is the stated estimator uncertainty (i.e. the sharpness)

    • dist (character + default("norm")) - the estimator distribution name (e.g. norm) parameterised by location and scale

    • calibration (numeric) - the calibration as determined by the SD of the probabilistic prediction (sharpness) / the SD of the true values distribution, overconfident is <1, and conservative is >1

    • adjust (character + default("link")) - method for adjusting for bias. Either link function adjustment of true values, or probit adjustment of PIT values

    Minimally grouped by: dist + link + calibration + adjust (and other groupings allowed).

    summarise

    produce the results as a groupwise summary or a prediction by prediction metric (default `TRUE` [logical])

    threshold

    If given calculates the threshold misclassification probability (default `NA` [numeric])

    Value

    a dataframe. columns depend on summarise

    Examples

    qs = seq(1, 199, 2) / 200
df = tidyr::crossing(
  true_value = 0,
  location = stats::qnorm(qs, 1, 1),
  scale = c(1 / 2, 1 / 1.5, 1, 1.5, 2),
  dist = "norm",
  link = "identity"
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(calibration = scale) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(dist, link, calibration)
df %>%
  prediction_scores() %>%
  dplyr::glimpse()
